sources.entry: MarkEdit - MarkEdit is a free and open-source Markdown editor, for macOS. It's just like TextEdit on Mac but dedicated to Markdown.

summary.one_liner: MarkEdit is a free, open-source Markdown editor for macOS that aims to be a lightweight, TextEdit-like app dedicated to Markdown.
summary.what_it_does: MarkEdit is a native macOS Markdown editor described as a roughly 4 MB installer that stays fast on very large files, with the README citing million-line files. It strictly follows the GFM specification and uses CodeMirror 6 for editing features such as multi-caret editing and code folding. The README says UI controls are native macOS, including force-touch word lookup, inline predictions, and Writing Tools. Customization is built around CSS, JavaScript, and CodeMirror extensions, and a built-in extension manager offers curated official extensions for things like Markdown preview, hiding syntax, themes, AI writing, and visual table editing. Shortcuts and AppleScript support are mentioned, and the README states the app does not collect user data.
use_cases: write and edit Markdown documents on a Mac
open and edit very large Markdown or text files
automate editor actions with Shortcuts or AppleScript
how_to_run: Download MarkEdit.dmg from the latest release on the GitHub releases page
Open the DMG and drag MarkEdit.app to Applications
Or install via Homebrew: brew install --cask markedit
notable: Installer around 4 MB, much smaller than Electron apps according to the README
Strict GFM compliance with no proprietary syntax
Native macOS controls including Writing Tools and inline predictions
Extensible via CSS, JavaScript, and CodeMirror extensions with a built-in extension manager
caveats: macOS only; the README lists supported older macOS versions from macos-12 through macos-15
The README says MarkEdit is intentionally minimal, so behavior changes are discussed before being accepted
